extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Congress, Patent Office officials, patent examiners, inventors, and interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Operational standards, procedural recommendations, and administrative criteria for the United States Patent Office (report of the Commissioner of Patents, 1877). Covers reproduction and printing of patents, classification and indexing, library needs, examiners' duties and hiring, models policy, trade-mark registration, and related fee/financial recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photolithographic reproduction of old patent drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproduce drawings of patents granted prior to 1871 by photolithographic process; preparatory tracing required; produce multiple copies for sale and office use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First step: trace original drawings with ink on muslin by hand. Preparatory work for about 100,000 old drawings to be completed by March 31, 1878; completion of 150 photolithographic copies of each drawing to follow. Drawings are arranged in portfolios by class, numbered, named, and dated to correspond with patents so they can be easily inspected. Photolithographic copies are sold to the public and yield annual proceeds (estimated ten to twelve thousand dollars). Recent fire destroyed and injured many sets; appropriation (~$30,000) recommended to reproduce lost sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing of specifications of patents granted prior to Nov. 20, 1866
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproduce and print manuscript specifications for patents issued before the government printed patents (pre-1867) to make them accessible and reduce cost/delay of manuscript copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At present manuscript certified copies are supplied at ten cents per folio (100 words) and require many copyists; printing would make the material accessible outside Washington and reduce litigation expense. An appropriation of $20,000 recommended to begin reproducing these specifications; sales would reimburse the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of printing to the Patent Office (in-house printing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform the printing of patent specifications within the Patent Office rather than relying on the Government Printing Office (GPO) to increase speed, accuracy, and reduce back-and-forth proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents are issued weekly and specifications must be printed promptly after fees are paid. Because specifications are legal documents requiring technical exactness, proofs frequently require consultation with Examiners; current practice requires additional proof-reading in the Office after GPO proofing, causing delays and repeated transport. If printing were done in the Office under immediate supervision of Commissioner and Examiners, work would be more expeditious, accurate, and could save money. In-house printing could also produce stock copies of old specifications at little additional expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of final fee to cover printing and photolithographing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the final patent issue fee to reflect actual government printing/photolithography costs so costlier patents do not subsidize simpler ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final fee historically $20 when only manuscript copies were provided; with printed specifications and drawings the government furnishes more. Cost of printing varies greatly between simple and complex cases. Remedy: add the cost of printing the specification and drawings to the final fee (estimate: final fee might be reduced to $15 plus printing cost to reimburse government). If models are not required (and more drawings are needed) the full fee might be retained. Any surplus could be used to print old specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of classified digests/abridgments of patents (British-style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish categorized abridgements that summarize patented inventions, arranged chronologically with subject-matter indexes to permit rapid state-of-the-art searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abridgements (as published in Britain) contain brief summaries of inventions by class and chronological order with subject indexes; the work would require 2–3 years and is best done under Patent Office supervision in connection with examination work. Indexes would allow rapid searches, save Office time and public expense, and help defeat enforcement of worthless patents of narrow scope. Distribution to public libraries is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette publication and dissemination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and expand the Official Gazette (weekly rescript of Patent Office transactions) with wider distribution and more favorable pricing to increase public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Gazette began in 1872; minimum price per annum is $5 for clubs, $6 for single subscribers. Commissioner believes price is too high and reduced rates for newsdealers or larger orders would increase circulation without reducing receipts. Members of Congress may name eight public libraries to receive the Gazette; increasing this number is recommended to benefit the public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office library collection development and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a comprehensive, up-to-date library (domestic and foreign patent specifications, scientific works, periodicals) with complete catalogues and subject indexes to support novelty examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library additions include duplicate English patents (1852–1876) and abridgments; a complete alphabetical and subject catalogue is being compiled. Many departments remain incomplete; at least 10,000 additional volumes recommended. Index foreign patents (French, Belgian, Italian, Austrian, Norwegian, German, etc.) and make yearly supplements. A well-classified, catalogued library with subject-matter indexes would greatly speed examinations and save the Office money. Recommend special appropriation (~$10,000) from surplus receipts for books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of inventions into classes and arrangement of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide subjects of invention into a fixed set of classes and arrange drawings and reproductions within those class portfolios to facilitate examination and public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For convenience, subjects are divided into 158 classes. Drawings of each class are numbered, named, and dated to correspond with patents and arranged in portfolios so they can be easily inspected during state-of-the-art examination. Proper arrangement permits immediate appreciation of the collection's value and supports sales of photolithographic copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' duty to judge novelty using library and indexed sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are legally required to determine novelty before issuing a patent and must rely on an up-to-date library and indexes, including foreign patent collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because novelty must be judged prior to granting a patent, Examiners need a library kept up to date; the absence of complete indexes or foreign sets hampers this duty. Improving library and indexing is essential to better quality patents and fewer filings in old fields of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-mark examination and classification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine and classify trade-mark applications using a systematic class-based scheme and facsimile arrangement analogous to patent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade-mark work is divided into nearly eighty official classes with facsimiles arranged accordingly. Examination and classification proceed on the same principles as patent examination. Increased appreciation of trade-marks' importance and recent legal remedies make careful classification and registration essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of original drawings for photolithography (tracing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare old patent drawings for photolithographic reproduction by tracing them with ink on muslin as the initial required process step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracing on muslin by hand is the first necessary step; this preparatory work for the set of old drawings (estimated at ~100,000) was expected to complete by March 31, 1878. Recent fire damage requires re-tracing some drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and correction workflow for printed specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure printed specifications are proofread with Examiner consultation and corrected in a workflow that minimizes reprinting and delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because specifications are legal documents, proof-sheets often require referring back to Examiners to correct errors. Current practice requires additional proof-reading in the Office after GPO proofing, causing back-and-forth. In-house printing would eliminate duplicate proofing and expedite accurate issue of patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive examinations for appointment and promotion of examining corps
rubrics_metrics.description: Use competitive written examinations focused on mechanical subjects and elementary physics (plus measured general efficiency) for appointing and promoting Patent Office examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 1869 appointments and promotions have been made by competitive examination; candidates for lowest grade are examined on mechanical subjects within observation range and some physics. Promotions consider both exam results and predetermined allowance for general efficiency. The system yields better-fitted persons and stimulates industry and study. Recommend statutory provision to permit holding examinations at stated periods across different parts of the country to avoid forcing candidates to attend in Washington.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on requiring and storing patented models
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-evaluate the requirement that inventors furnish models, balancing their evidentiary and illustrative value against cost to inventors and storage burdens on the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models have been accumulated since 1836, filling available space and incurring cost in furnishing, storing, and exhibiting. Models serve for public examination, court evidence, and reissue references, but the collection imposes heavy space and restoration costs (evidenced by fire damage). Commissioner suggests that under certain conditions it may be better to dispense with models or alter the requirement; distribution of rejected duplicates to institutions has been done previously as a space-management practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model and record preservation and restoration procedures after disaster
rubrics_metrics.description: When models and photolithographic copies are damaged (e.g., by fire/water), undertake preservation, restoration, and careful salvage procedures to retain evidence and reduce replacement cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the September 24 fire, efforts included surveying burned halls, retaining every scrap, arresting rust by taking apart and oiling water-damaged models, trimming charred photolithograph sets to salvage them, and restoring what is practicable. Congress appropriated funds ($45,000) for restoration; estimates of salvageable models (~5,000–10,000) and photolithograph set restoration costs (~$30,000) were made. Priority given to valuable and intricate models and to restoring useful photolithograph sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and distribution of rejected or duplicate models
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispose of or distribute rejected, duplicate, or less useful patented models (e.g., give to scientific institutions) to reduce storage burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously some rejected models were distributed to scientific institutions. This practice reduced accumulation. Given space constraints, continued or expanded distribution of duplicates or rejected models is a management option to relieve storage needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of foreign patent duplicates and indexes to examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure duplicate sets of foreign patents and their indexes and place duplicates in examiners' rooms to facilitate examination and digest compilation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A duplicate set of English patents and abridgments (1852–1876) was obtained from the British Government; duplicate indexes allow copies to be placed in Examiners' rooms and facilitate completing digests by class down to date. Similar indexing of French and Belgian patents is in progress and should be extended to other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales strategy and pricing for reproductions and Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Price and market photolithographic copies, printed specifications, and the Official Gazette at moderate rates and create distribution channels (libraries, newsdealers) to increase circulation and recover costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photolithographic copies sale proceeds already amount to $10–12k per year. Printing and selling old specifications would be remunerative; offering the Gazette to newsdealers at a lower rate for bulk orders could increase circulation without reducing receipts. Establishing stock copies (e.g., 50 additional printed copies) could reduce repeated manuscript copying expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent fund surplus receipts for Office improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply surplus receipts from patent fees to strategic Office investments like library acquisitions and reproduction/repair of lost records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipts for the past year exceeded expenditures (not including printing) and a portion of surplus should be appropriated for library purchases (~$10,000) and for reproduction of lost drawings/specifications. The report documents balances and recommends applying surplus to these capital needs.
